acceptance: With the option set on a DataFrame platform and DuckDB 2.x, the sketch operations in the write-primitives DataFrame workload run and report their real status; a test shows the option reaches `execute_operation` as true.
Without the option they report SKIPPED with a reason that names the option the DataFrame platform accepts; a test covers it, and shows no repository statement is issued.
`benchbox run --dry-run` output for a DataFrame platform shows the option when set, consistent with how `duckdb` shows it.

The write-primitives README states the option applies to DataFrame platforms too. Any generated or advertised option listing checked by `tests/unit/platforms/test_advertised_platform_options.py` passes.
`make batch-member-check TESTS=<tests added or changed>` passes; `make comment-policy-check` reports nothing for the touched files.
A `changelog.d/` fragment describes the new option on DataFrame platforms.
context: 2026-11-12 18:25: PR #4175 merged to develop as 6ab8a3d979 (DuckDB bound <3.0.0, lock on 2.0.0). The precondition for this item now holds.
description:
Problem. On DuckDB 2.x the datasketches extension installs only from a third-party repository, and BenchBox requires `--platform-option allow_third_party_extensions=true`, registered for the `duckdb` and `ducklake` platforms (PR #4175). The DataFrame SQL-parity workload in `benchbox/core/write_primitives/benchmark.py` (`_execute_dataframe_sql_parity_workload`) runs sketch operations on an internal `DuckDBAdapter` and passes `allow_third_party_extensions=False`, because DataFrame platforms do not register the option. On 2.x those operations are therefore always SKIPPED and a user has no way to enable them.

Owner decision 2026-11-13: register the same option for the DataFrame platforms that run this workload and forward it to the internal adapter. Default stays off.

Decision gate (member, before editing): trace how a `--platform-option` reaches a DataFrame adapter (`_OPTION_SPEC_ROWS` in `benchbox/platforms/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/cli/test_platform_options_reach_adapters.py`, an existing DataFrame option such as Polars `rechunk`). If forwarding fits inside the frozen scope, build it. If it needs a path outside the scope, stop and report the path; do not fall back silently.

Frozen scope: `benchbox/core/write_primitives/*`, `benchbox/platforms/__init__.py`, `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/*_df.py`, `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/benchmark_mixin.py`, `benchbox/utils/duckdb_extensions.py`, `benchbox/cli/*`, `tests/unit/core/write_primitives/*`, `tests/unit/cli/*`, `tests/unit/platforms/test_*`, `tests/unit/utils/test_duckdb_extensions.py`, `docs/*`.

Guardrails (members of batch df-platform-followups):
- Stay inside the frozen scope below; a path outside it is refused at landing. If the work needs another path, stop and report it.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Search for an existing helper before adding one (`make duplicate-check-delta`).
- Do not edit SQL text, reference answers, expected-result fixtures or baselines to make a check pass.
- Members make no tracker write, open no PR, do not run the fast tier, benchmarks or timing runs, and never force heavy-work admission. They use absolute paths under their own worktree and stop at a landing report.
- One `changelog.d/` fragment per member.
- No third-party repository is contacted, and `allow_extension_repositories` is not touched, unless the option is explicitly true.
- Adapter SDK imports stay lazy. DuckDB 1.x behaviour is unchanged.
- Do not edit `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/expression_family.py`, `pandas_family.py` or `unified_frame.py`; another member owns them.
